title: Cap. III Resp. Rat. 2: deny the split — end-intention causes means; Paul/grace
pass_a_gloss: Response. This discrimination between physical and moral means, which Vasquez desires to establish, we in no way admit. For according to the order of intention (about which the question now is) the end is the cause of means, both moral and physical: and from the preceding desire of the end these means are both chosen and applied. The rule is well known: Means are applied in order to the end. Therefore the intention of the end always precedes the supplying of the means. For God would not have destined efficacious grace to Paul unless he had first efficaciously destined to give him glory.
pass_b_english: Resp. We do not grant Vasquez's physical/moral split at all. In the order of intention (the real question) the end causes the means — moral as well as physical — and from desiring the end first those means are chosen and applied. Known rule: means are applied toward the end. So intending the end always comes before supplying the means. God would not have destined efficacious grace to Paul unless he had first efficaciously destined to give him glory.
source_text: Resp. Hoc discrimen inter media physica & moralia, quod Vasques cupit stabilire, nullo modo admittimus. Nam secundum ordinem intentionis (de quo jam quaeritur) finis est causa mediorum tam moralium quam physicorum: atque ex praecedente finis desiderio media haec tum eliguntur tum adhibentur. Nota est regula, Media adhibentur in ordine ad finem. Finis itaque intentio semper praecedit suppeditationem mediorum. Non enim Deus destinasset Paulo efficacem gratiam, nisi prius efficaciter destinasset dare illi gloriam.
